{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.4 (TrueLink Hosting, Interface Licence and Support Agreement)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review — verified findings and negotiation posture

---

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against the playbook and verified 19 findings. Eight rules are compliant or better than our preferred position — notably there is **no audit right** against us, **no non-compete**, **no non-solicit**, **no liquidated damages or termination fee**, **no MFN burdening us**, a renewal mechanic that already beats our fallback (1-year renewals, 30-day opt-out), and a Vendor-granted most-favoured-rate undertaking plus one-year price freeze in § 6. Governing law (California / San Luis Obispo County, §§ 26–27) sits at our fallback and is not redlined.

The risk is concentrated in the **allocation of liability and IP**. Three critical deviations sit at or across the walk-away line:

- **Liability (§ 12, p0077):** TrueLink is capped at 12 months' hosting and support fees while our liability, including a broad indemnity, is **entirely uncapped** — expressly walk-away territory. Only carve-outs are TrueLink's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
- **Indemnity (§ 12):** nominally mutual, but there is **no Vendor IP infringement indemnity anywhere** in the document and no duty to defend, while our indemnity covers our breach, our customers' acts, the Web Site and product liability with knowledge qualifiers stripped.
- **IP ownership (§ 2(d)):** ownership runs one way to TrueLink. Nothing gives us ownership of, or an enduring licence to, what TrueLink builds for us; our licence terminates with the Agreement.

Two further items materially constrain us commercially: **§ 3(i)** imposes a de facto sole-supplier obligation to order every credit report from TrueLink for the full term, with no service-level exit (walk-away), and **§ 5(a)** imposes unconditional minimum monthly fees with § 6 stripping our right to contest them. There are also two clean gaps — **no transition assistance or data return** on exit, and **no insurance obligation** at all despite TrueLink hosting our Web Site and processing Credit Data.

## Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 12 Indemnity (p0071–p0075) |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 2 Licence (§ 2(d); cf. §§ 8(d), 13) |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | § 12 Indemnity (p0077) |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 15 (in § 12 Indemnity outline block) |
| 5 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 2 Licence / § 3(i) (p0042) |
| 6 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | §§ 13–14 (p0078–p0079) |
| 7 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties on Customer | Compliant | §§ 5–8, 12–14 |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 2 Licence (§ 2(a), p0022/p0024) |
| 9 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume | Deviation | § 5 Compensation (§ 5(a); § 6) |
| 10 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | §§ 9, 11 (cf. disclaimer p0076) |
| 11 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | §§ 13–14 (p0078–p0079) |
| 12 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 5 Compensation / § 6 |
| 13 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant (fallback) | §§ 26–27 |
| 14 | Medium | MFN — MFN burdening Customer | Compliant | § 5 / § 6 (p0047) |
| 15 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 8 Covenants and Warranties of Client |
| 16 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 13 (p0078) |
| 17 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | Sections 13–30 (p0078–p0097) |
| 18 | Low | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 2 Licence (§ 2(a), (c); § 15) |

## Walk-away items

These must move before signature:

1. **Uncapped Customer liability against a capped Vendor (§ 12, p0077).** Our fix is the fallback, not the preferred position: make the existing 12-month fee cap mutual and agreement-wide, and carve indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct out of the cap. We have not pressed the preferred USD 1,000,000 floor, the mutual consequential-damages exclusion, or data-protection/fraud/IP carve-outs; those remain available if negotiation reopens.
2. **No Vendor IP infringement indemnity and no duty to defend (§ 12).** We add a TrueLink defend-and-indemnify obligation for IP infringement, breach of law, TrueLink-caused data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, with notice, control-of-defence and cooperation mechanics, and narrow our own indemnity to Client Content and our violations of law.
3. **De facto sole-supplier obligation (§ 3(i), p0042).** Every credit report for a borrower underwritten through a System using the Interface must be ordered from TrueLink, for the full term, uncapped and with no exit if TrueLink misses the § 3(b) response-time or § 3(d) availability standards. Shortest cure: make the sourcing commitment permissive.
4. **TrueLink's 30-day non-renewal notice (§ 13, p0078).** Below our 90-day floor. We split the mutual notice so TrueLink gives 90 days while our 30-day right is preserved.
5. **No insurance of any kind** where TrueLink hosts our Web Site and processes Credit Data and Client Content. We insert a new Section 31 at preferred levels (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber/privacy USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request), which also carries the fallback E&O and cyber minima.

## Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the eight deviations and two missing clauses: liability cap mutuality and carve-outs; Vendor indemnity plus narrowing of ours; new § 2(e) on ownership, assignment of work product, perpetual licence-back to embedded TrueLink IP and retention of our data; permissive credit-report sourcing; express Client termination for convenience and 90-day Vendor non-renewal notice; assignment successor carve-out and reasonableness standard; § 5(a) minimums limited to the current 12-month term with a 30-day reduction right and true-up; Vendor conformance warranty (12 months software / 90 days Services) with repair, re-performance or refund; transition assistance and data return in § 14; and new § 31 insurance.
2. **Sequence the negotiation** around the five walk-away items first; the remaining deviations are single-clause conforming edits.
3. **Diligence two cross-references:** the undefined "Non-Competition Agreement" cited in § 8(d) (it operates in our favour here, but we should confirm it imposes nothing on us), and the open-ended "not less than ____ months" Support Services period in Section 4, which § 14 makes a condition of our termination right and could extend the § 5(a) lock-in beyond twelve months.
4. **Confirm two repaired findings** (T4C and WARRANTY) on the final drafted text before the redline goes out.
5. **Note for the business team:** § 6's one-year price freeze and most-favoured-rate undertaking, and the absence of any audit right, non-compete, non-solicit or termination fee, are all in our favour and should not be reopened."}
